canonical_statement: For 1 <= p < infinity and a nonnegative function u in W^{1,p}(R^n) that vanishes at infinity, its symmetric decreasing rearrangement u* belongs to W^{1,p}(R^n) and the L^p norm of its weak gradient is no greater than that of u.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: Candidate only: integral (x : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n)), norm (fderiv/weakGradient (symmetricDecreasingRearrangement u) x) ^ p <= integral x, norm (weakGradient u x) ^ p

domain_and_universes: Provisional analytic scope: n : Nat with 1 <= n; p : Real with 1 <= p and p < infinity; u : R^n -> R, nonnegative, in W^{1,p}(R^n), vanishing at infinity; Prop in Lean universe 0. Exact mathlib types are not frozen at intake.
hypotheses: u vanishes at infinity: every positive superlevel set has finite measure
conclusion: u* is in W^{1,p}(R^n) and integral |grad u*|^p <= integral |grad u|^p

alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent after nonnegativity and finite-p norm conventions

excluded_degenerate_cases: The intake excludes p = infinity, signed-function formulations not explicitly reduced through |u|, equality characterization, anisotropic rearrangements, and arbitrary rearrangements. Dimension zero and functions whose positive superlevel sets have infinite measure are outside the frozen human claim.
